title: Investigation of manual therapy effects in low back pain
summary: Manual therapy is a hands-on treatment that is often used in people with back and other musculoskeletal pain. However, it is still unclear how much of its benefit comes from the physical treatment itself and how much is influenced by factors such as a patient’s expectations or the information they receive about the treatment. In this study, 84 adults with long-term low back pain will be assigned to one of three groups. One group will receive manual therapy along with an explanation of the treatment and its purpose. A second group will receive the same treatment, but it will be described only as a routine mobility assessment. A third (control) group will only take part in assessment sessions. Researchers will assess pain during back movement, sensitivity to pressure, and spinal mobility immediately before and after the treatment session or rest period. Participants’ expectations and previous experiences with treatment will also be recorded. The results will help determine whether the benefits of lumbar spinal mobilization are mainly due to the physical treatment itself or are partly influenced by the treatment context. This could help clinicians provide manual therapy in a more effective and transparent way.
conditions: Self-reported low back pain for at least 3 months

interventions.name: In the open-treatment (OT) group, participants will receive lumbar spinal mobilization while lying prone on a treatment plinth. In the control group (CT), no intervention will be performed between assessments. The overall study duration will be approximately 60 minutes for one visit.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Self-reported low back pain fulfilling all of the following sub-criteria:
a.	Localization criterion: Pain located in the anatomical region between the inferior margin of the 12th rib and the inferior gluteal folds, with or without radiation to the lower extremities.
b.	Chronicity criterion: Pain duration of at least 3 months.
c.	Persistence criterion: Pain present on at least 50% of days during the preceding 6-month period.
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Diagnosed osteoporosis or spondylolisthesis 
2.	Spondylodesis at any level in the lumbar spine
3.	Acute low back pain related to recent tissue injury
4.	Acute post-surgical pain
5.	Skin lesions, inflammation, or infection at the site of testing
6.	Diagnosed neurological disorders affecting sensory or motor function
7.	Diagnosed severe or uncontrolled cardiovascular disease
8.	Diagnosed severe psychiatric disorders that may interfere with informed consent or study participation
9.	Professional education or occupation indicating advanced knowledge of manual therapy techniques
10.	Current enrolment as a physiotherapy student
